methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
RISE Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing startup founded by Arron Acosta and Blake Sessions, has raised $22M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, including later-stage peers Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), and Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), alongside earlier-stage Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a $44M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $1.7B implied value, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The divergence reflects the composition of the peer set, which skews toward more mature Series B rounds.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $37M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $872M. Material uncertainty attaches to stage-appropriate peer selection: the peer set includes three Series B valuations that may overweight RISE's pre-revenue or early-revenue profile relative to more mature competitors. Stage-progression methodology, by contrast, may undervalue the company if product-market traction exceeds typical Series A progression patterns. Revenue, unit economics, and customer concentration would refine this range materially.
